record.paper_title: Initial boundary value problem for Korteweg-de Vries equation: a review and open problems
record.original_question: For the finite-interval Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0 with initial data u(x,0)=φ(x) and general boundary conditions B_k u = h, determine whether the system is controllable under completely general boundary conditions, beyond the specific boundary-control configurations B_{1,0}, B_{2,0}, and B_{4,0} discussed in the paper.

evidence.quote: Thus, with respect of the control issue, a natural and interesting open problem arises here:
• Is the IBVP (4.18), with general boundary condition, controllable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Korteweg–de Vries equation on a finite interval (0,L), L>0,
    u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0,   (x,t) ∈ (0,L) × (0,T),
with initial datum
    u(x,0) = φ(x),  x ∈ (0,L),
and three (linear) boundary conditions of the general form
    B_k u(t) = h_k(t),   k = 1,2,3,  t ∈ (0,T),
where each B_k is a linear boundary operator built from the traces of u, u_x, u_{xx} at x = 0 and x = L, chosen so that the resulting initial-boundary value problem is well-posed in a suitable Sobolev space on (0,L). One or more of the boundary data h_k are designated as boundary controls.

Question. Determine, for an arbitrary admissible (well-posed) choice of boundary operators B_1, B_2, B_3 — beyond the specific Dirichlet/Neumann-type configurations classically known to be controllable — whether the system is exactly (or null) controllable: that is, whether for every pair of states (φ, ψ) in the chosen function space (with ψ sufficiently close to φ in the case of local controllability), there exist controls h_k among the boundary data such that the corresponding solution satisfies u(·,T) = ψ. Characterize, in terms of the boundary operators (B_1, B_2, B_3) and the length L, when controllability holds and when it fails.
artifact.status_search_result: Controllability of KdV on a finite interval has been established for several specific boundary configurations (Rosier; Cerpa; Coron; Glass–Guerrero; and others), and recent work has resolved small-time local controllability at all critical lengths for Neumann boundary control. However, no general controllability theory covering arbitrary admissible (Colin–Ghidaglia type) boundary operators has been published; recent literature on coupled KdV systems explicitly notes that controllability is highly sensitive to the boundary configuration and that general results are not available. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Boundary effects on the controllability of coupled KdV systems
status_evidence.snippet: coupled KdV systems are very sensitive to the choice of boundary conditions; existing results do not directly extend to new configurations
status_evidence.claim: Controllability for KdV-type systems depends strongly on the boundary configuration, and general results are not yet available.

status_evidence.title: Small-time local controllability of a KdV system for all critical lengths
status_evidence.snippet: gives a complete answer to the longstanding open problem on small-time local controllability of KdV on all critical lengths
status_evidence.claim: Recent work resolves a specific case (Neumann boundary control, critical lengths), confirming the broader general-boundary problem remained open until at least 2025.

status_evidence.title: Control of a Korteweg-de Vries equation: A tutorial
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of boundary controllability results for KdV on a bounded interval, focused on standard boundary configurations
status_evidence.claim: Existing surveys treat specific boundary configurations rather than general boundary operators.
